# Self Learning by Perspire AI

> Free, self-paced lessons for 10th-grade chemistry, math and world history. Each lesson has a short reading, step-by-step animations, a video, and homework help whose answers are revealed one step at a time. No account is needed.

The three subject sites are single-page apps: lesson, chapter and homework views are reached through `#` links on the subject pages. Outside lesson videos (Khan Academy, Tyler DeWitt, CrashCourse and others) are embedded from YouTube and remain with their creators.

## Subjects

- [Chemistry](https://perspireai.com/chemistry/): organized by chapter, with animated lessons, quick checks, and a narrated video for every Chapter 1–3 lesson plus Chapter 2 and 3 exam-review videos. Chapter 1, Measurement & Reference Sheets: metric prefixes; conversion factors; temperature (°C and K); reading the class periodic table. Chapter 2, Atomic Theory & Nuclear Chemistry: models of the atom; atomic structure and isotopes; average atomic mass; waves and light; photons (E = hν); the Bohr model and bright-line spectra; nuclear equations; half-life. Chapter 3, Electron Configuration & Periodic Trends: blocks and families; Aufbau, Pauli and Hund; longhand and shorthand configurations with the Cr/Cu exceptions; ion configurations; atomic and ionic radius; ionization energy and electronegativity. Chapter 4, Lewis Structures & Nomenclature: valence electrons; the periodic table; Lewis dot structures; chemical bonds; the CO₂ Lewis structure; VSEPR shapes and polarity; naming covalent compounds; naming ionic compounds (Types I–III); naming any compound with the nomenclature flowchart (acids, bases, diatomic elements, alkanes).
- [Chemistry: periodic table](https://perspireai.com/chemistry/#/periodic-table): interactive table showing each element's group, valence electrons and Lewis symbol.
- [Chemistry: worksheet help](https://perspireai.com/chemistry/#/worksheets): step-by-step answers for every chemistry worksheet: conversion practice (Chapter 1); wave calculations, nuclear equations, half-life and the Unit 2 exam review (Chapter 2); orbital diagrams, electron configurations, periodic trends and the Unit 3 exam review (Chapter 3); and the VSEPR, covalent naming and ionic naming (Types I–III) worksheets plus a nomenclature flowchart tool (Chapter 4).
- [World History](https://perspireai.com/history/): AP World History, one chapter a day (Bentley & Ziegler, Traditions & Encounters, Chapters 10–24, c. 2200 BCE – 1800 CE). Every chapter has a big question, an interactive timeline, an animated map, a short lesson with cause-and-effect chains, flashcards, a narrated video, and AP-style practice with primary sources, short answers and an essay outline.
- [World History Chapter 10: Mediterranean Society: The Greek Phase](https://perspireai.com/history/#/chapter/10): c. 2200 – 31 BCE. How did small, quarrelsome Greek city-states shape the whole Mediterranean, and how did Alexander spread Greek culture as far as India?
- [World History Chapter 11: Mediterranean Society: The Roman Phase](https://perspireai.com/history/#/chapter/11): c. 2000 BCE – 117 CE. How did a small town on the Tiber River come to rule the whole Mediterranean, and why did it trade its republic for an emperor?
- [World History Chapter 12: Cross-Cultural Exchanges on the Silk Roads](https://perspireai.com/history/#/chapter/12): c. 200 BCE – 600 CE. What traveled along the Silk Roads besides silk, and why did the great classical empires collapse?
- [World History Chapter 13: The Expansive Realm of Islam](https://perspireai.com/history/#/chapter/13): 570 – 1258 CE. How did a faith born in a desert trading town become a civilization stretching from Spain to India in about a century?
- [World History Chapter 14: The Resurgence of Empire in East Asia](https://perspireai.com/history/#/chapter/14): 589 – 1279 CE. How did the Sui, Tang and Song rebuild a unified China, and why did Korea, Vietnam and Japan borrow so much from it?
- [World History Chapter 15: India and the Indian Ocean Basin](https://perspireai.com/history/#/chapter/15): c. 500 – 1500 CE. How did a politically divided India become the hub of a vast Indian Ocean trading world?
- [World History Chapter 16: The Two Worlds of Christendom](https://perspireai.com/history/#/chapter/16): c. 330 – 1100 CE. Why did the Christian world split into a rich Byzantine east and a rebuilding Latin west?
- [World History Chapter 17: Nomadic Empires and Eurasian Integration](https://perspireai.com/history/#/chapter/17): c. 1000 – 1450 CE. How did nomadic herders, above all the Mongols, build the largest land empire in history, and how did it knit Eurasia together?
- [World History Chapter 18: States and Societies of Sub-Saharan Africa](https://perspireai.com/history/#/chapter/18): c. 500 – 1500 CE. How did trade across the Sahara and the Indian Ocean create rich African kingdoms and city-states?
- [World History Chapter 19: The Increasing Influence of Europe](https://perspireai.com/history/#/chapter/19): c. 1000 – 1350 CE. How did western Europe go from a poor, divided region to one that was growing, trading and crusading?
- [World History Chapter 20: Worlds Apart: The Americas and Oceania](https://perspireai.com/history/#/chapter/20): c. 950 – 1500 CE. How did the Aztecs, the Inca and the peoples of Oceania build complex societies with little or no contact with Afro-Eurasia?
- [World History Chapter 21: Reaching Out: Expanding Horizons of Cross-Cultural Interaction](https://perspireai.com/history/#/chapter/21): c. 1200 – 1500 CE. How did travelers, merchants, the plague and the Ming treasure fleets connect the world, and set the stage for European voyages?
- [World History Chapter 22: Transoceanic Encounters and Global Connections](https://perspireai.com/history/#/chapter/22): c. 1400 – 1800 CE. How did European voyages across the oceans tie every inhabited region of the world together for the first time?
- [World History Chapter 23: The Transformation of Europe](https://perspireai.com/history/#/chapter/23): 1500 – 1800 CE. How did religious wars, new kinds of states and the Scientific Revolution transform Europe between 1500 and 1800?
- [World History Chapter 24: New Worlds: The Americas and Oceania](https://perspireai.com/history/#/chapter/24): 1492 – 1800 CE. How did European conquest, disease and colonial economies remake the Americas and reach into Oceania?
- [World History: master timeline](https://perspireai.com/history/#/timeline): every chapter's events on one interactive timeline, with what was happening elsewhere in the world.
- [Math](https://perspireai.com/math/): organized by unit. Now available: Units 0–5, from lines and piecewise functions through quadratics, conic sections, polynomials, and radicals.
- [Math Unit 0: Linear, Absolute Value & Piecewise Functions](https://perspireai.com/math/#/unit-0): five narrated video lessons (lines review, linear inequalities and interval notation, absolute value functions, graphing piecewise functions, writing piecewise functions with domain and range) with homework help for HW #1–#6 and the Day 4–5 notes.
- [Math Unit 1: Quadratic Functions](https://perspireai.com/math/#/unit-1): five narrated video lessons (graphing in standard form, transformations and vertex form, characteristics, intercept form, writing quadratic functions) with homework help for HW #1–#7 and the Day 1–5 notes.
- [Math Unit 2: Solving Quadratics, Systems & Inequalities](https://perspireai.com/math/#/unit-2): six narrated video lessons (the quadratic formula, the discriminant and complex numbers, completing the square, linear–quadratic systems, quadratic–quadratic systems, quadratic inequalities) with homework help for HW #11–#19 and the Day 11–18 notes.
- [Math Unit 3: Conic Sections](https://perspireai.com/math/#/unit-3): eight narrated video lessons (circles, parabolas with focus and directrix, writing circle and parabola equations, ellipses, writing ellipse equations, hyperbolas, writing hyperbola equations, classifying conics) with step-by-step animations and homework help for HW #1–#8.
- [Math Unit 4: Polynomial Functions](https://perspireai.com/math/#/unit-4): fourteen narrated video lessons (polynomial basics, zeros and linear factors, long division, synthetic division, factoring, solving polynomial equations, function operations and composition, solving by graphing, end behavior, the Rational Root Theorem, irrational and complex roots, the Fundamental Theorem of Algebra, polynomial inequalities, inverse functions) with homework help for HW #1–#17.
- [Math Unit 5: Radical Expressions](https://perspireai.com/math/#/unit-5): three narrated video lessons (simplifying radicals, multiplying radicals, dividing radicals and rationalizing the denominator) with homework help for HW #1 and both Fall Final Exam Review packets (linear equations, conics, polynomials, quadratics, complex numbers).
